children: Egypt's D Developments has announced plans to invest up to 15 billion Egyptian pounds ($269 million approximately) in four real estate projects in Obour City following its launch through an Egyptian-Saudi investment partnership.
The newly established developer is backed by Egyptian investors and Saudi Arabia's Al-Hokail Group.
D Developments will initially focus on Obour City, where it plans to build a portfolio of four projects targeting different segments of the local property market, the company said in a statement.
The statement did not disclose the ownership stakes of Egyptian and Saudi shareholders or the expected launch dates of the four projects.

Ahmed Kassem, CEO of D Developments, said the developer would prioritise project locations and property types based on market demand, with further details on individual developments to be announced in phases.

Sheikh Ibrahim Al-Hokail, representative of Al-Hokail Group, said the decision to enter Egypt's property market followed an assessment of investment opportunities and demand arising from urban development.
He said Obour City was selected because of its established infrastructure, existing population and demand for residential and commercial property.
The partnership combines Al-Hokail Group's investment experience in Saudi Arabia with the Egyptian partners' expertise in real estate development, engineering consultancy and local market conditions.
(Writing by Eman Hamed; Editing by Anoop Menon)
